source: RM0490 Rev 6 SS4.7; drafted from STM32C031.svd
verified: 2026-08-24. Same two-chain split as peripherals.stm32c0.rcc.json, applied honestly rather than uniformly. (1) Bits/offsets: mechanically drafted from STM32C031.svd. (2) Reset value: ACR's reset word 0x00040600 is PARTIALLY corroborated, not wholesale SVD-only and not wholesale independently checked -- say which bits are which rather than one blanket claim. LATENCY=000 and ICEN=1 (2 of the 5 defined bits in this reset word) ARE independently corroborated against RM0490 prose: SS4.3.2 states plainly 'Upon power-on reset ... the LATENCY[2:0] bitfield [is set] to 000', and SS4.3.3 states 'The Instruction cache memory is enabled after system reset' -- both self-consistent paragraphs (appeared directly under their own headings, not the shifted-heading range this chapter otherwise suffers from). DBG_SWEN=1, EMPTY=0, ICRST=0 and PRFTEN=0 (the remaining 3 defined bits) are SVD-only -- no independent RM sentence was found asserting their reset states, so treat those specifically as less-corroborated than LATENCY/ICEN, not as equally checked. ACR.LATENCY's SPIN BEHAVIOUR (distinct from its reset value) traced against stm32c0xx_hal_rcc.c:670/775 (HAL_RCC_ClockConfig, not the flash driver -- RCC polls flash latency, not FLASH's own HAL). CR.STRT's kind independently re-verified against this chip's own SVD field description per team-lead's steer (see strt_kind_verification below), not carried over from the design doc unchecked.
scope_note: FLASH_SR/FLASH_CR/FLASH_OPTR/PCROP/WRP (the program/erase interface) are NOT part of this regmap's registers[] -- no HAL_FLASH_* call appears on the reset-to-blinking-LED path for stock firmware. FLASH_CR.STRT is analysed below anyway (not added to registers[]) because team-lead specifically asked it be checked as a load-bearing example for kind 5 self-clearing.

registers.name: ACR
registers.reset_decoded: DBG_SWEN=1, EMPTY=0, ICRST=0, ICEN=1, PRFTEN=0, LATENCY=000

fields.name: LATENCY
fields.why: THE second of the three boot-critical spins. stm32c0xx_hal_rcc.c HAL_RCC_ClockConfig:670 writes the target latency then does 'while ((FLASH->ACR & FLASH_ACR_LATENCY) != FLatency)' -- same field written then re-read, not two different fields, so this is plain rw (kind mirrors would misdescribe it: mirrors is for a DIFFERENT field reflecting a written value, per the doc's SS1.3; here the field mirrors itself, which needs no special kind at all -- a plain rw store-then-readback terminates the loop on the very next read with zero extra modelling). RM0490 Table 14 (SS4.3.2, self-consistent prose, VERIFIED): HCLK<=24MHz->LATENCY=000 (1 HCLK cycle), HCLK<=48MHz->LATENCY=001 (2 HCLK cycles) -- only two legal settings on C0 (smaller than larger STM32 families). A stock 48MHz SystemClock_Config must set LATENCY=001 before SYSCLK exceeds 24MHz; this is the value the line-670 loop waits to see, and HAL_RCC_ClockConfig:775 does the symmetric wait when LOWERING frequency (drop latency only after the switch, not before).

fields.name: ICEN
fields.why: Instruction cache enable, reset=1 ('The Instruction cache memory is enabled after system reset', RM SS4.3.3, self-consistent paragraph). Performance-only, not polled.

fields.name: EMPTY
fields.why: Set by hardware from actual flash CONTENT (whether the first 64 bits read all-1s), but ALSO directly software-writable per RM SS4.3.4 ('The software can also modify the EMPTY flag directly'). Read-purity is violated because correct hardware-path behaviour needs the simulator's flash-content store, which the regmap engine (per the design doc SS3) does not own -- flagged here rather than silently omitted since it's still nominally inside a `regmap:` peripheral (FLASH) whose other fields ARE plain data; per the doc's granularity ruling (SS1.8, field-level hw deferred until it hurts) this is exactly the 'one impure register in an otherwise-data peripheral' case the doc says not to act on yet. Left in this file as documentation, not wired into registers[]'s field list, so the regmap engine sees only the pure fields (LATENCY/ICEN/PRFTEN/ICRST/DBG_SWEN) and this one is a known future gap rather than a silent wrong answer.

strt_kind_verification.asked: team-lead's steer: 'ADCAL and flash STRT are now doing the load-bearing work for kind 5 [self-clearing] ... verify them against the C0 HAL rather than assuming they inherited correctly from the doc.'
strt_kind_verification.register: FLASH_CR.STRT (bit 16, offset 0x014 -- not in this file's registers[] per scope_note, checked as a standalone verification)
strt_kind_verification.method: Read STM32C031.svd's own <description> for the STRT field directly (XML, not RM prose, no extraction-caveat risk) and cross-checked against every FLASH_CR_STRT usage in the fetched stm32c0xx_hal_flash_ex.c.
strt_kind_verification.svd_text_verbatim: "Start erase operation. This bit triggers an erase operation when set. This bit is possible to set only by software and to clear only by hardware. The hardware clears it when one of BSY1 and BSY2 flags in the FLASH_SR register transits to zero."
strt_kind_verification.hal_cross_check: grepped stm32c0xx_hal_flash_ex.c for FLASH_CR_STRT: two hits, both 'FLASH->CR |= FLASH_CR_STRT' / 'FLASH->CR = (... | FLASH_CR_STRT | ...)' -- SET only, never a matching CLEAR_BIT anywhere in the file. Software only ever turns it on; nothing in HAL turns it off.
strt_kind_verification.verdict: CONFIRMED self-clearing (kind 5), exactly as the doc's amended §1.5 states. Software-set/hardware-cleared-on-completion, with the SVD's own text independently corroborating the doc's classification -- no correction needed here, unlike the ESP32 TIMG case esp-soc caught. Also independently spot-checked ADCAL (STM32 ADC calibration bit, not this chip's minimum register set): SVD text 'set by software to start... cleared by hardware after calibration is complete' -- same pattern, also CONFIRMED, not carried over from memory.
